identity.scenario: docker unavailable while previous generation serves

what: Inspector silently showed old routes and API reference after a failed development reload.
expected: Keep working routes visible and display a persistent reload error with its cause and recovery steps.
observed: The live routes page showed connected and one hello route despite many failed reloads; diagnostics returned no errors.
root_cause: apps/inspector/app/inspector-shell.tsx used only the active child graph connection for status. Failed reloads belong to the CLI supervisor; the active child diagnostics remain empty. No shell component consumed retained dev.generation.failed logs or startup failures.
fixed_by: Added a global failure banner backed by retained supervisor logs. It explains the previous version is serving, provides Docker-specific recovery, correlates startup errors to the failed build window, links filtered error logs, and clears on a later dev.generation.active record. Supporting-detail failures do not hide the main failure. Verified against the real logistic-platform-3 backend in the source Inspector. Ordinary and genuinely prepared CLI startup both passed failed-edit retention, visible errors, typed .env repair, new routes/OpenAPI, and automatic banner clearing without refresh under the same dev PID. The real app now exposes all 34 application paths plus 30 auth paths.
reproduction: Observe a failed reload while the previous hello backend stays active.
Open the routes page; the original Inspector shows connected without explaining the failure.
Open the edited source Inspector against the same backend; assert failure cause and stale routes notice.
Follow View error logs and inspect the same startup failure; check 390px viewport for overflow.

before.note: Original routes page had no reload failure warning.

after.note: Real startup failure and stale API warning.
Real app routes visible in patched source Inspector on 3210.

browser.assertion: The failed-reload banner includes real startup errors, leaves hello routes visible, and opens error-filtered logs. Live localhost:3210/routes now includes company routes and has no failed-reload banner.
steps: Open routes with the same backend.
Assert alert, retention error, stale-docs notice and existing route.
Follow error logs and verify the retention detail.
Reject DAYS=invalid, preserve old response, then repair DAYS=30 with a new route under the same ordinary/prepared dev PID.
Assert route visibility and banner clearing without refreshing.
Verify all 34 application OpenAPI paths and 30 auth paths in the restarted real app.

regressions.assertion: 390px layout has no horizontal overflow and recovery text remains visible.
Next compilation and runtime errors are empty.
ordinary: same-PID failed edit and typed recovery, new route/OpenAPI, automatic warning clearing, joined owned-process shutdown.
prepared: same-PID failed edit and typed recovery, new route/OpenAPI, automatic warning clearing, joined owned-process shutdown.

limitations: Changes are local and unpublished; full repository acceptance/release packaging were not run.
Standalone Scalar reference HTML is outside the Inspector shell.
Focused strict TypeScript comparison retains the same 10 pre-existing dependency errors with no introduced errors.
The source Inspector startup deadline is now fixed and verified with CLI-owned startup and recovery; see related report bf-3da7c773d109b45a19e71179.

notes: 100 unit tests and 69 focused tests passed. New fast regressions live in the existing merge-blocking unit gate; browser recovery is chained into test:inspector:browser.
Disposable ordinary and prepared apps, their Inspector processes, browsers, listeners, and owned descendants were joined and removed.
Docker became unavailable again before restart; reopened Docker, then confirmed docker ps and application startup succeeded. No authored app files or persisted data were deleted.

Superseding live verification: source CLI PID 90959 owns both backend and Inspector on 3000/3210. The separate Inspector was stopped. The live proxy and backend expose matching 34 application plus 30 auth paths. Stop the authorized dev owner with kill -TERM 90959. See bf-3da7c773d109b45a19e71179 for current process proof.
